title: Chip-scale packaged in-line polarization-resolved detector for optically pumped magnetometers
task: Develop chip-scale packaged in-line polarization-resolved detector for optically pumped magnetometers
key_results: Wire grid polarizer PER 25.3 dB at 795 nm; CSP detector 29.6 dB CMMR, 8.4×10⁻⁵ degree/Hz^0.5 angular resolution; SERF OPM achieves 33.5 fT/Hz^0.5 sensitivity at 10 Hz

title: Emergent surface magnetic ordering and surface electronic dipole layers in a two-dimensional spin=1/2 La2CuO4 film
task: Characterize surface magnetic ordering and electronic structure in ultrathin La2CuO4 films
key_results: Emergent surface magnetic ordering at room temperature with temperature-dependent hysteresis; Cu2+/Cu1+ mixture with strong magneto-electronic coupling via upper Hubbard band

task: Develop flexible active-matrix micro-LED display with ferroelectric 1T-1FeMFET pixel architecture
key_results: Record normalized memory window of 0.63 V/nm; on/off ratio 4×10⁸; retains performance after 10⁵ bending cycles at 4 mm radius; 428 ppi resolution with 0.68 nW dynamic power consumption

key_results: 9% total conversion efficiency (637.2 nm to 1588.3 nm); pump noise 154 Hz; SNR up to 117.8 at 327.7 kHz input rate; predicted fidelity >52% over 100 km transmission

title: Transition between cooperative emission regimes in giant perovskite nanocrystals
task: Characterize transition between superfluorescence and amplified spontaneous emission in giant perovskite nanocrystals
key_results: Superfluorescence observed below 45 K; amplified spontaneous emission dominates above 100 K; temperature and excitation density drive regime transition; cooperative phenomena analyzed across temperature range
comments: Clear experimental demonstration of collective emission regime switching, though temporal coherence requirements and role of structural disorder in determining transition boundaries merit further investigation.

model_io.model: Thin film of giant CsPbBr₃ perovskite nanocrystals

hypotheses.hypothesis: Temperature and excitation density control transition from temporally-coherent superfluorescence to incoherent amplified spontaneous emission
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; clear regime transition between 45–100 K with SF at low T, ASE at high T and high excitation

title: Interlayer exciton flux amplification driven by strong exciton confinement
task: Amplify interlayer exciton flux via nanoscale bandgap confinement in van der Waals heterostructures
key_results: ~8,300% diffusion current amplification vs conventional microscale gating; flux enhancement decoupled from total IX population; governed by nanoscale density gradient
comments: Remarkable amplification via nanoscale confinement opens reconfigurable exciton circuits; practical integration with active nanocavity arrays and scalability to device arrays merit exploration.

model_io.model: Van der Waals heterostructure with electro-plasmonic nanocavity

hypotheses.hypothesis: Nanoscale bandgap gradient confines IXs, creating density profile whose outward diffusion exceeds electric drift, amplifying flux

key_results: SrTiO₃ capping suppresses localization in both insulator-like and metal-like SrIrO₃; critical thickness for MIT reduced to <3 u.c. (SIO_i) and 2 u.c. (SIO_m); lattice relaxation mitigates intrinsic disorder

task: Elucidate strain-tunable inter-valley scattering as universal mobility enhancement mechanism in 2D TMDs
key_results: Tensile strain enhances n-type mobility via K–Q valley separation; compressive strain improves p-type mobility via Γ–K decoupling; tuning rates exceed silicon; full-band transport model quantitatively matches experiments

hypotheses.hypothesis: Strain modulates mobility in TMDs primarily through inter-valley scattering changes rather than effective mass renormalization
